proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(i=I(m)\) for the latent target of intervention label \(m\).  We first recover the common support.  The vector \(Y^{(0)}\) is a nondegenerate Gaussian in \(\mathbb R^n\): \(A\) is invertible by full-column-rank mixing and every diagonal entry of \(\Omega_0\) is positive.  The determinant of the matrix formed from \(n\) independent copies of \(Y^{(0)}\) is a nonzero polynomial, whose zero set has Lebesgue measure zero.  Hence the corresponding copies of \(X^{(0)}=UY^{(0)}\) span \(\mathcal S\) almost surely and
\[
 \Pr_P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}})=1.
\]
The canonical-frame rule is deterministic in \(\mathcal S\), so it returns exactly \(U\) on this event.  The construction of \(\mathsf C\) performs no inversion for \(r<r_0\).  Since \(N_{r_0}\ge n\), the same determinant argument, a finite union over environments, and a countable union over \(r\ge r_0\) show that all later empirical covariance matrices are positive definite almost surely.  Thus every permitted inverse is an \(n\)-dimensional inverse.

For simultaneous covariance coverage, define
\[
 W_{m,r}=\Sigma_m^{-1/2}S_{m,r}\Sigma_m^{-1/2}-I_n.
\]
For a fixed unit vector \(v\), \(N_rv^{\top}(W_{m,r}+I_n)v\) has the \(\chi^2_{N_r}\) law.  Its moment generating function and Chernoff's inequality give
\[
 \Pr\!\left(\left|\frac{\chi^2_N}{N}-1\right|>
 2\sqrt{t/N}+2t/N\right)\le2e^{-t}.
 \tag{1}
\]
A maximal \(1/4\)-separated subset of the unit sphere is a \(1/4\)-net and has at most \(9^n\) elements, by the disjoint-ball volume argument.  For symmetric \(W\), approximation of a maximizing Rayleigh quotient by this net gives
\[
 \|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max_{v\text{ in the net}}|v^{\top}Wv|.
 \tag{2}
\]
Apply (1)--(2) with \(t=t_r\), take a union over the net and the \(n+1\) environments, and use \(\|\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa\).  This produces events \(\mathcal C_r\) satisfying
\[
 \Pr_P(\mathcal C_r^c)\le\alpha2^{-r-1},\qquad
 \max_{m\in\mathcal E}\|S_{m,r}-\Sigma_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le a_r.
 \tag{3}
\]
The retained prefixes may be nested; no independence between stages is used.  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal C=\bigcap_{r\ge r_0}\mathcal C_r,qquad
 \Pr_P(\mathcal C)\ge1-
 \sum_{r\ge r_0}\alpha2^{-r-1}\ge1-\alpha.
 \tag{4}
\]

We next identify the population ranges that the observable matrices encode.  In latent coordinates, let \(b_i\) be row \(i\) of \(B^{(0)}\), let \(\epsilon_i=Z_i-b_i^{\top}Z\), and write the observational and reset variances as \(\omega_i>0\) and \(\widetilde\omega_i>0\).  Cancellation of all unchanged conditional densities in the intervention-to-observation likelihood ratio yields
\[
 \nabla_z\log\frac{p_m^Z(z)}{p_0^Z(z)}
 =-\frac{\epsilon_i}{\omega_i}b_i+
 \left(\frac{\epsilon_i}{\omega_i}-\frac{z_i}{\widetilde\omega_i}\right)e_i.
 \tag{5}
\]
The disturbance \(\epsilon_i\) is independent of its parental predictor.  If \(b_i\ne0\), that predictor has positive variance and the two coefficients in (5) have nonsingular covariance; if \(b_i=0\), the variance reset \(\widetilde\omega_i\ne\omega_i\) makes the coefficient of \(e_i\) nondegenerate.  Transforming scores under \(Y=AZ\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{col}(R_m)=A^{-\top}\operatorname{span}\{e_i,b_i\}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The range of a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices is the span of their ranges, because its null space is the intersection of their null spaces.

If \(V\) is ancestral, (6) gives
\[
 \operatorname{col}(R(V))=A^{-\top}\operatorname{span}\{e_i:i\in V\}.
 \tag{7}
\]
For \(k\in V\), if \(k\) is a leaf of the induced graph, no remaining parent vector has a nonzero \(k\)-coordinate, and \(\operatorname{rank}R(V\setminus\{k\})=|V|-1\).  If \(k\) is not a leaf, a remaining child contributes a parent vector with a nonzero \(k\)-coordinate; subtracting the already present other coordinate directions recovers \(e_k\), and the rank is \(|V|\).  Removing a leaf preserves ancestry.  Induction shows that the public smallest-label rule removes the smallest labelled leaf at each step, and reversing the removal order gives the population topological order.

In a graph loop, the recorded set \(D_t\) is descendant-closed by induction.  The set \(V_j\setminus D_t\) is therefore ancestral.  The same leaf calculation shows that deleting \(\pi_t\) either deletes its dual coordinate, when no surviving child exists, or leaves that coordinate in the range, when a surviving child exists.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}projector\mbox{-}geometry}\) makes the projector product zero exactly in the latter case.  The update of \(D_t\), first in increasing \(j\) and then in decreasing \(t\), records exactly all descendants.  Consequently the population graph output is
\[
 \operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G_{\mathcal E})
 =I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I.
 \tag{8}
\]

Now work on \(\mathcal C\) at a stage satisfying \(a_r\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}covariance\mbox{-}to\mbox{-}correlation}\) gives, for every queried set \(M\),
\[
 b_M:=\|\widehat R_r(M)-R(M)\|_{\mathrm{op}}le |M|e_r.
 \tag{9}
\]
If \(b_M\le g_0/4\), the min--max formula and \(|v^{\top}(\widehat R_r(M)-R(M))v|\le b_M\) show that each ordered empirical eigenvalue is within \(b_M\) of its population counterpart; the promised spectrum \(\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)\) therefore certifies the exact rank.  Let \(P_M\) and \(\widehat P_M\) project onto the population positive range and the empirical eigenvectors above \(g_0/2\).  Projection of the perturbed invariant-subspace equation onto \(\operatorname{null}(R(M))\), followed by the equal-rank projector identity obtained from the singular-value decomposition of their cross-Gram matrix, gives
\[
 \|\widehat P_M-P_M\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{b_M}{g_0-b_M}\le\frac{2b_M}{g_0}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The identical bound holds for null projectors.  Hence, for the empirical graph comparison \(\widehat c_{t,j}\), the product triangle inequality gives
\[
 |\widehat c_{t,j}-c_{t,j}(P)|
 \le\frac{2(b_{V_t}+b_{M_{t,j}})}{g_0}
 \le\frac{4ne_r}{g_0}.
 \tag{11}
\]
If all previous decisions agree with the population transcript, the next query is an occurrence of \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\).  The two reached-band assumptions therefore apply at that query.  Equations (9)--(11), the smallest-certified-zero rule, and induction through each restarted order and graph loop prove that every completed empirical transcript is the population transcript.  No condition has been invoked for a subset absent from that transcript.

For a singleton, (10) with its sharper denominator gives
\[
 \|\widehat P_m-P_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\frac{e_r}{g_0-e_r}.
\]
For a unit empirical-range vector \(\widehat v_m\), normalize \(P_m\widehat v_m\) when \(e_r<g_0/2\).  The elementary normalization inequality then gives
\[
 \|\widehat v_m-v_m\|_2
 \le2\|(I-P_m)\widehat v_m\|_2
 \le\frac{2e_r}{g_0-e_r}\le\frac{4e_r}{g_0}.
 \tag{12}
\]
When \(e_r\ge g_0/2\), the same displayed upper bound follows from the distance at most two between unit vectors and the nonempty range in (6).  Map these vectors isometrically into \(\mathcal S\) by \(U\) and stack the rows.  Then
\[
 \|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|\widehat H-H^{\star}\|_{\mathrm F}
 \le\frac{4\sqrt n\,e_r}{g_0}.
 \tag{13}
\]
If \(v_m=A^{-\top}q_m\), (6) says that \(q_m\) is supported on target \(I(m)\) and its parents, and
\[
 (v_m^{\top}U^{\top})G=v_m^{\top}A=q_m^{\top}.
\]
After relabelling by \(I\), this is precisely the zero pattern required in \(\mathrm{def{:}encoder\mbox{-}loss}\).  Thus (13) bounds \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H,P)\).

It remains to verify the corrected terminal cap.  Put \(b=b_{\star}\), \(q=q_{\star}\), \(u=u_{\star}\), and \(B=B_{\mathrm{samp}}=2^{r_B}\).  Since \(b\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\),
\[
 q=\frac{64\kappa^2}{b^2}\ge256\kappa^4\ge256,
 \qquad u\ge\log(16q)>4.
\]
Also \(u\ge t_0\ge n\log9\), so \(32qu\ge n\).  The power-of-two definition and \(qu>1\) yield
\[
 32qu\le B<2\lceil32qu\rceil\le64qu+2<66qu.
 \tag{14}
\]
Because \(t_{r_B}=t_0+\log(2B)\), (14) gives
\[
 t_{r_B}<t_0+\log(132qu)
 =u+\log\!\left(\frac{132}{16}u\right)\le2u.
 \tag{15}
\]
The last inequality follows because \(u>4\) and the increasing function \(x-\log((132/16)x)\) is already positive at \(x=4\).  Combining \(B\ge32qu\) with (15),
\[
 \frac{t_{r_B}}{B}\le\frac1{16q}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Using \(\sqrt q=8\kappa/b\), (16), and \(b\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\), we obtain the quantitative slack
\[
 a_{r_B}
 \le4\kappa\left(\frac1{4\sqrt q}+\frac1{16q}\right)
 =\frac b8+\frac{b^2}{256\kappa}
 \le\frac{65}{512}b<\frac b7.
 \tag{17}
\]
Therefore
\[
 e_{r_B}=40\kappa^4a_{r_B}<\frac{40\kappa^4b}{7}
 \le\frac{e_{\star}}7.
 \tag{18}
\]
In particular,
\[
 ne_{r_B}<\frac{g_0h_0}{112}\le\frac{g_0}{112},
 \qquad
 \frac{4ne_{r_B}}{g_0}<\frac{h_0}{28},
 \qquad
 \frac{4\sqrt n\,e_{r_B}}{g_0}<\frac{\tau}{7}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Thus every rank and comparison interval strictly separates its two promised bands and the encoder gate holds.  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{sup}}\cap\mathcal C\), whose probability is at least \(1-\alpha\) by (4), the procedure returns by stage \(r_B\), (8) is its graph, and (13) gives its encoder loss.  The sample accounting is \(B_0=n+B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) in the observational environment, at most \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) in each intervention environment, and \(B_{\mathrm{tot}}=n+(n+1)B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) in total.

Put \(\epsilon=2^{-n}\).  The structural matrix of \(\mathfrak F_n\) has nonzero rows only at labels \(3\) and \(4\), with parent vectors \(b_3=(1,1)\) and \(b_4=(1,1+\epsilon)\).  Thus \(B^2=0\) and \(\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|B\|_{\mathrm F}<3\); deleting any one target row preserves these properties.  Since \((I-B^{(m)})^{-1}=I+B^{(m)}\) and each intervention-noise covariance has spectrum in \([1,2]\),
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_m)
 \le2\|I+B^{(m)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2<32,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_m)
 \ge\|(I+B^{(m)})^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{-2}>1/16.
 \tag{20}
\]
Hence every fixed-coordinate covariance has spectrum in \([1/32,32]\).  The construction directly verifies the linear Gaussian DAG equations, graph compatibility, perfect single-target variance resets, and full-rank mixing with \(G=I_n\); independent streams can be sampled in all environments.

For a reset root,
\[
 R_i=\frac14e_ie_i^{\top}.
 \tag{21}
\]
For a child with parent vector \(b\), write \(s=b^{\top}(Z_1,Z_2)\) and \(E=Z_c-s\).  Under the observational law, \(s\) and \(E\) are independent and the score difference is \(d_c=(-bE,(E-s)/2)\).  Therefore, on the parent plane and coordinate \(c\),
\[
 R_c=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 bb^{\top}&-b/2\\
 -b^{\top}/2&(1+\|b\|_2^2)/4
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{col}(R_c)=\operatorname{span}\{b,e_c\}.
 \tag{22}
\]
In the orthonormal basis \(b/\|b\|_2,e_c\), put \(B_0=\|b\|_2^2\in[2,5]\).  The nonzero block has determinant \(B_0^2/4\) and trace \((5B_0+1)/4\), so
\[
 \lambda_{\min}^{+}(R_c)
 \ge\frac{B_0^2}{5B_0+1}\ge\frac4{11},
 \qquad
 R_c\succeq\frac4{11}P_{\operatorname{span}\{b,e_c\}}.
 \tag{23}
\]

Every nonempty subset of the four core labels other than \(\{3,4\}\) has positive eigenvalues at least \(1/40\).  Root-only sets have gap \(1/4\), and child singletons have gap at least \(4/11\).  If a set contains one root \(i\) and a child with parent vector \(b\), then
\[
 \lambda_{\min}^{+}(P_{e_i}+P_b)
 =1-|e_i^{\top}b|/\|b\|_2
 \ge1-2/\sqrt5>1/10.
\]
Multiplying by \(\min\{1/4,4/11\}=1/4\) gives a parent-plane lower bound greater than \(1/40\), while (23) supplies the child coordinate with coefficient \(4/11\).  Adding the other child preserves that bound and supplies its orthogonal child coordinate; adding the other root gives the direct parent-plane bound \((1/4)I_2\).  These cases exhaust the core subsets other than \(\{3,4\}\).  Every label at least \(5\) contributes an orthogonal eigenvalue \(1/4\).

The population leaf-removal order is
\[
 (3,4,1,2,5,6,\ldots,n),
\]
so the reversed topological order is \(\pi=(n,n-1,\ldots,5,2,1,4,3)\).  In the first order round, deleting one label retains a core root whenever both children remain; after label \(3\) is removed, no later order query contains both children.  In any graph query containing both children, both core roots already lie in the prefix, descendant deletion removes no root, and deletion of the current row removes at most one root.  Singleton encoder queries contain only one child.  Thus no reached occurrence has core intersection exactly \(\{3,4\}\).  The preceding subset bounds prove that every reached positive eigenvalue is at least \(1/40\).

For every graph query, descendant pruning leaves an ancestral set.  Removing the current label deletes its coordinate exactly when it is a leaf; otherwise (22) lets a remaining child's parent vector supply the coordinate.  Both ranges are consequently coordinate subspaces, so their projector-product norm is zero or one.  This proves the reached projector band with \(h_0=1/2\), using actual projectors rather than the source's printed angular expression.

The order phase evaluates \(\sum_{t=2}^nt=n(n+1)/2-1\) matrix occurrences.  The graph phase contributes \(n-1\) prefix occurrences and \(n(n-1)/2\) comparison-sum occurrences, and the encoder phase contributes \(n\) singletons.  Hence the total is
\[
 n(n+1)/2-1+(n-1)+n(n-1)/2+n=n^2+2n-2.
 \tag{24}
\]

For the unqueried subset, the four vectors \(e_3,b_3,e_4,b_4\) are independent because \(\det(b_3,b_4)=\epsilon\ne0\).  Thus \(R(\{3,4\})\) is positive definite on the four-dimensional core.  With \(v=(1,-1,0,0)^{\top}/\sqrt2\), (22) gives
\[
 v^{\top}R_3v=0,
 \qquad
 v^{\top}R_4v=\epsilon^2/2.
\]
The Rayleigh variational principle yields
\[
 \eta^{\ast}(P)
 \le\lambda_{\min}^{+}(R(\{3,4\}))
 \le\epsilon^2/2=2^{-2n-1}<1/80.
 \tag{25}
\]
Since \(G=H=I_n\), \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), while \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\).

Finally, every Gaussian density and every causal conditional is strictly positive and continuously differentiable.  Let \(\phi_v\) denote the centered Gaussian density of variance \(v\).  A root intervention has a nonconstant ratio of centered Gaussian densities.  For a child, differentiating
\[
 \frac{\phi_2(z_c)}{\phi_1(z_c-b^{\top}z_{\mathrm{pa}(c)})}
\]
in either parent coordinate gives a nonzero function because both parent coefficients are nonzero.  Hence the source's Assumption 1 parent-ratio condition holds, and a perfect stochastic intervention is a legal special case of its smooth soft-intervention model.  Entrywise laws of large numbers give \(S_{m,r}\to\Sigma_m\) in probability.  On the uniformly positive-definite neighborhood,
\[
 S_{m,r}^{-1}-\Sigma_m^{-1}
 =S_{m,r}^{-1}(\Sigma_m-S_{m,r})\Sigma_m^{-1}
\]
gives inverse convergence, and multiplication by a Gaussian vector of finite second moment gives the source's squared-mean score-difference consistency.  Thus all promised-class assumptions and all stated non-margin source conditions hold.  Equations (20), (24), and (25) establish every remaining assertion.

On the stated Gaussian variance-reset subclass, equation (22), as recorded in \(\mathrm{def{:}source\mbox{-}margins}\), gives
\[
 \lambda_i(R(M))\in\{0\}\cup[g_0,\infty)
 \quad\text{for every }M\subseteq[n].
 \tag{26}
\]
It therefore gives the reached eigen band in particular.  The separately required condition \(c_{t,j}(P)\in\{0\}\cup[h_0,1]\) is the reached projector band.  The Gaussian structural, intervention, mixing, conditioning, and sampling conditions in the statement are exactly the remaining member properties of \(\mathrm{def{:}promised\mbox{-}class}\).  Hence
\[
 P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa),
\]
and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}promised\mbox{-}transcript\mbox{-}certificate}\) applies.  This derivation used Gaussian covariance identities and therefore proves no upward transfer to the source's larger smooth soft-intervention class.

For the converse-to-necessity statement, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}separation\mbox{-}family}\) proves, for every \(n\ge4\),
\[
 \mathfrak F_n\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(1/40,1/2,32),
 \qquad
 \eta^{\ast}(P)\le2^{-2n-1}<1/80.
 \tag{27}
\]
It also proves directly that \(\mathfrak F_n\) has smooth positive causal conditionals, one legal distinct single-target intervention per node, the parent-ratio property in Assumption 1, and the required score consistency.  Thus it is a member of the published model class, not merely of a newly constructed analogue.  The positive certificate recovers it from its reached bands by Theorem 1, while (27) violates the fixed equation-(22) threshold \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\).  One legal published-class witness that is recoverable while violating a proposed condition proves that the condition is not necessary for recoverability over that class.

The projector qualification is algebraic.  Biorthogonality gives \(H_{i,:}G_{:,i}=1\), so Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\ge1,
\]
whereas every product of orthogonal projectors has operator norm at most one.  These quantities therefore cannot satisfy the printed general identity when the norm product is strictly larger than one.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}projector\mbox{-}geometry}\) instead proves the valid reciprocal lower bound \(\rho_i(G)\) for a witnessed nonzero comparison.  No step above uses the false printed identity.

theorem.statement: The answer is affirmative for post-summary computation.  Let \(Q=8(n^2+2n)\).  For outward rational enclosures of the exact fixed-coordinate empirical covariance summaries, refined to the selected working precision, and, when an ambient encoder is requested, an outward rational enclosure of \(U\), all of total input length \(L\), the capped procedure \(\mathsf C_{\mathbb Q}\) assigns at most \(e_{\star}/(4Q)\) arithmetic enclosure error to each reached operation, has total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\) within every restarted transcript, and certifies every inverse, rank, zero-versus-positive spectral split, repeated invariant subspace, projector product, and largest-singular-value comparison used by \(\mathsf C\).  On every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\), it terminates on every input by the cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\), returning either \(\bot\) or a finite answer, and with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) it returns a non-abstaining answer satisfying \(\widehat{\mathcal G}=I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H,P)\le\tau\).  With logarithms of reciprocals truncated below at zero, its working precision and post-summary Boolean running time are polynomial in \(L,n,\log\kappa,\log(1/g_0),\log(1/h_0),\log(1/\alpha),\log(1/\tau)\).  No separation among repeated positive eigenvalues is required.  If computation begins from the raw streams rather than their summaries, reading and summarizing the data incurs in addition at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) input-record operations; thus no end-to-end running-time claim polynomial only in logarithmic gap parameters is made.
theorem.proof_tex:
Let \(Q=8(n^2+2n)\) and \(\beta=e_{\star}/(4Q)\).  In any one restarted transcript, the public program has \(n^2+2n-2\) reached matrix occurrences.  Adding \(n+1\) covariance inversions, \(n\) primitive formations, at most two projector constructions and one product-norm computation per graph comparison, and \(n\) singleton selections is bounded by \(Q\).  Assign the \(j\)-th operation in that restart a numerical enclosure radius
\[
 \varepsilon_j\le\beta,
 \tag{28}
\]
and, for the operation's own decision, reduce it further to the minimum of \(\beta\) and the required fixed fraction of \(g_0\), \(h_0\), \(1/\sqrt n\), or \(\tau/n\).  Then, deterministically,
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^{Q}\varepsilon_j\le Q\beta=e_{\star}/4.
 \tag{29}
\]

We first justify rational covariance algebra.  Clear denominators in an input covariance matrix.  Its integer entries have bit length at most \(O(L)\).  The Leibniz determinant formula has at most \(n!\) products of \(n\) such entries, so every determinant minor has bit length \(O(n(L+\log n))\).  Fraction-free elimination therefore decides positive definiteness and, when the matrix is invertible, computes its adjugate-over-determinant inverse with polynomially many operations on polynomial-bit integers.  Sums and the three-factor primitive formula increase numerator and denominator lengths only polynomially in \(L\) and \(n\).  Outward rounding every entry to \(p\) fractional bits gives operator error at most \(n2^{-p}\), because the operator norm is at most the Frobenius norm.  The min--max formula and the quadratic-form bound used in (9) transfer this operator radius to every ordered eigenvalue.  Thus primitive and eigenvalue enclosure error at most any prescribed \(\xi>0\) is obtained with
\[
 p=O\!\left(L+\log n+\log(1/\xi)\right).
 \tag{30}
\]
This contains, and sharpens for exact rational centers, the prior covariance-to-primitive partial result.  If the input itself is an outward interval rather than an exact rational center, the condition \(\lambda_{\min}(S_{m,r})\ge(2\kappa)^{-1}\) and the resolvent identity give the previously established additional inverse error \(4\kappa^2n2^{-p}\), and the primitive error is at most \(Cn\kappa^4 2^{-p}\); adding \(O(\log\kappa)\) bits in (30) absorbs it.

The nonalgebraic radius terms also have certified rational enclosures at polynomial cost.  A square root of a nonnegative rational is bracketed by bisection, and range reduction writes a positive rational as \(2^jy\) with \(y\in[1,2)\).  With \(z=(y-1)/(y+1)\in[0,1/3]\),
\[
 \log y=2\sum_{\ell=0}^{s}\frac{z^{2\ell+1}}{2\ell+1}+r_s,
 \qquad
 0\le r_s\le\frac{2z^{2s+3}}{(2s+3)(1-z^2)}.
\]
The same series at \(z=1/3\) encloses \(\log2\).  Thus \(O(p+L)\) rational terms suffice for \(p\) output bits, with explicit tail sign and magnitude; outward rounding gives certified values of \(t_r\) and \(a_r\) in polynomial Boolean time.

Rank certification does not require eigenvectors.  For a rational symmetric matrix \(K\) and rational \(x\), exact fraction-free symmetric elimination gives a rational block \(LDL^{\top}\) congruence of \(K-xI\).  Congruence preserves the maximal dimensions of positive and negative quadratic-form subspaces, so the signs of the one- and two-dimensional diagonal blocks determine the inertia and hence the number of eigenvalues below \(x\).  Bisection between rational endpoints gives outward eigenvalue intervals of width \(\xi\) in \(O(\log((1+\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}})/\xi))\) inertia calls.  The determinant-minor bound above proves polynomial bit growth in every call.  At the terminal stage, (18)--(19) from Theorem 1 give, for every reached \(M\),
\[
 b_M\le ne_{r_B}<g_0/112.
 \tag{31}
\]
Choosing the rational rounding radius below \(g_0/112\), the inertia counts certify that every empirical eigenvalue lies either in the zero cluster below \(g_0/28\) or in the positive cluster above \(27g_0/28\).  They consequently certify the population rank and the public forbidden band.  On an off-promise input, failure of these inequalities produces \(\bot\), not a rounded rank.

It remains to obtain whole invariant subspaces without separating eigenvalues inside a cluster.  At a certified occurrence let \(k\) be the inertia count of the empirical zero cluster.  If \(k=0\) or \(k=n\), the relevant projector is exactly \(I_n\) or \(0\).  Otherwise the only gap used is
\[
 \widehat\lambda_{k+1}-\widehat\lambda_k
 \ge g_0-2b_M>g_0/2.
 \tag{32}
\]
Moreover, when \(a_r\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\),
\[
 \|S_{m,r}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\kappa,
 \quad
 \|S_{0,r}^{-1}-S_{m,r}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4\kappa,
 \quad
 \|\widehat R_r(M)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le24n\kappa^3.
 \tag{33}
\]
For a nonempty promised class, every singleton is nonzero by the variance reset and \(\|R_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4\kappa^3\), so \(g_0\le4\kappa^3\).  Let \(K_0\) be the least power of two not smaller than \(32n\kappa^3\), so \(K_0<64n\kappa^3\).  Scale \(\widehat R_r(M)-g_0I_n/2\) by \(K_0\).  Its norm is at most one and its separating gap is at least \(g_0/(128n\kappa^3)\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certified\mbox{-}hermitian\mbox{-}projector}\), with \(S=I_n\), computes the projector onto the entire lower cluster to operator error \(\delta\) in Boolean time polynomial in
\[
 n,\quad \log\kappa,\quad \log(1/g_0),\quad \log(1/\delta).
 \tag{34}
\]
This invocation remains valid when eigenvalues are repeated within either cluster, because (32), not an internal eigengap, is its premise.  Converting rational entries to directed dyadics first changes the matrix by at most \(n2^{-p}\).  Projecting the perturbed invariant-subspace equation across the gap in (32), exactly as in (10), adds at most \(4n2^{-p}/g_0\) to the projector radius.  Choosing \(p\) from (30) absorbs this term into \(\delta\).

Let \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) be the two exact empirical positive-range projectors in a graph comparison, and let \(\widetilde P_1,\widetilde P_2\) be rational approximations with operator errors at most \(\delta\).  Outward-rounded multiplication gives
\[
 \|\widetilde P_1(I-\widetilde P_2)-P_1(I-P_2)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\delta+\delta^2+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mult}}.
 \tag{35}
\]
Choose the three local radii so that the right-hand side is at most \(\min\{\beta,h_0/16\}\).  For a rational matrix \(D\), the Hermitian dilation
\[
 \mathcal H(D)=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&D\\D^{\top}&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
has largest eigenvalue \(\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Exact rational inertia of \(\mathcal H(D)-xI\), followed by bisection, therefore encloses that largest singular value to any additive \(\xi\) with polynomially many polynomial-bit operations.  The norm is one-Lipschitz, so enlarging this interval by the right-hand side of (35) certifies the exact empirical projector-product norm.  By (19), its statistical distance from the population comparison is less than \(h_0/28\).  Taking \(\xi\le h_0/16\) leaves total distance less than \(h_0/4\), which separates \(0\) from \([h_0,1]\).  The path induction of Theorem 1 then proves that all finite-precision rank and graph decisions equal those of \(\mathsf C\).

For the encoder, let \(\widehat P_m\) be a nonzero empirical singleton projector and let \(\widetilde P_m\) satisfy \(\|\widetilde P_m-\widehat P_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta\).  Since \(\operatorname{tr}(\widehat P_m)\ge1\), some coordinate obeys \(\|\widehat P_me_j\|_2\ge1/\sqrt n\).  Choose a column of \(\widetilde P_m\) with maximal certified norm.  If \(\delta\le1/(8\sqrt n)\), its norm is at least \(7/(8\sqrt n)\).  Directed rational square-root and division enclosures produce a vector whose distance from the empirical range is at most \(3\sqrt n\,\delta\).  Denote the stacked, frame-mapped output by \(\widehat H_{\mathbb Q}\).  Repeating the normalization argument of (12) and stacking rows yields
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{enc}}(\widehat H_{\mathbb Q},P)
 \le\frac{4\sqrt n\,e_{r_B}}{g_0}+8n\delta.
 \tag{36}
\]
If an outward rational frame is used for the ambient map, its operator contribution is added to the second term.  Choose all selector, normalization, and frame radii so that their total contribution is at most \(\tau/2\).  Equation (19) bounds the first term by \(\tau/7\), so (36) is strictly below \(\tau\).

Set every occurrence accuracy to the minimum specified after (28).  Equations (30), (34), and the inertia-bisection count show
\[
 p_{\mathrm{bit}}\le
 \operatorname{poly}\!\left(L,n,\log\kappa,
 \log(1/g_0),\log(1/h_0),\log(1/\alpha),\log(1/\tau)\right),
\]
where logarithms of reciprocals are truncated below at zero.  Indeed, \(\log(1/e_{\star})\) is bounded by the displayed logarithms and \(O(\log n+\log\kappa)\); on a nonempty promised class, \(g_0\le4\kappa^3\) controls the opposite scale.  Each restart has only \(Q=O(n^2)\) calls.  There are at most \(1+\log_2 B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) sampled stages, and the corrected definition makes \(\log B_{\mathrm{samp}}\) polynomial in the displayed logarithmic parameters.  Thus the complete post-summary Boolean cost has the asserted polynomial dependence.  Arithmetic intervals from a failed restart are discarded, so (29) is the relevant total for every transcript capable of returning.  Each finite rational call terminates.  The cap forces a final \(\bot\) on unresolved input, while on the event of probability at least \(1-\alpha\) from Theorem 1, (31)--(36) certify the correct graph and an encoder within \(\tau\) by \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}\).  Finally, if raw data rather than the covariance summaries are the input, merely reading the records costs \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\), before covariance formation; this proves the stated computational-scope qualification.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \((K,S)\) be an \(r\)-dimensional Hermitian definite pencil with \(\|K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1\) and \(\|S^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1\). If the ordered eigenvalues have gap \(\delta_k=\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k>0\), then for every \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\) there is a deterministic finite-precision algorithm returning a matrix \(\widetilde\Pi_k\) with \(\|\widetilde\Pi_k-\Pi_k\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon\), where \(\Pi_k\) projects onto the invariant subspace of the \(k\) smallest eigenvalues, using Boolean complexity polynomial in \(r\), \(\log(1/\delta_k)\), \(\log(1/\epsilon)\), and the logarithm of the condition number of \(S\).

prose_updates.tldr: As an exact-real statistical procedure on the declared linear Gaussian variance-reset class, the certificate returns the environment-labelled transitive closure \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and an environment-indexed encoder estimate within \(\tau\) of the parent-supported population range class, or abstains. project_justification.fill: The project supplies an anytime-valid exact-real Gaussian recover-or-abstain certificate with public reached gaps, a sharper cap \(B_{\mathrm{samp}}<66q_{\star}u_{\star}\), environment-labelled graph and encoder targets, and explicit encoder error bars. The resulting per-environment dependence is quadratic in \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear in \(\log(1/\alpha)\), rather than the anchor paper's RKHS fourth-power accuracy dependence. It also supplies a deterministic polynomial-bit post-summary realization with total arithmetic enclosure error at most \(e_{\star}/4\). prose_updates.related_work: Acartürk et al. (2024) are the strict finite-sample comparator. Their Section 5 equation (22) takes a positive-eigenvalue minimum over all subset sums, while printed equation (23) and Lemma 10 identify a projector-product quantity with \(\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). The latter norm product is at least one by biorthogonality even though a projector-product norm is at most one, so the present proofs use the actual subspaces and the valid reciprocal witness bound \(\rho_i(G)\), never the printed identity. The positive certificate is a covariance-specialized result for the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass and is not a strengthening on the source's full smooth soft-intervention class. The explicit Gaussian family is nevertheless legal in that published class and satisfies Assumption 1 and its other non-margin conditions; its recovery with exponentially small off-transcript \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\) shows only that equation (22) is not necessary. The Gaussian rate has quadratic \(1/\tau\) and essentially linear \(\log(1/\alpha)\) dependence, whereas the anchor's RKHS analysis has fourth-power accuracy dependence. Sobczyk (2025), Corollary 4.5 of arXiv version 2, supplies the deterministic certified spectral-projector primitive; the present theorem adapts it to the zero/positive cluster gap, adds exact rational inertia for rank and projector-product singular-value tests, and budgets their composed error along the adaptive transcript. Varıcı et al. (2025) provide the population score-range program, and Squires et al. (2023) validate the legal linear intervention substrate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The numerical theorem is a post-summary result: it assumes outward rational enclosures of the exact fixed-coordinate empirical covariance summaries and, for a rational ambient encoder, a supplied enclosure of the canonical support frame. Processing raw observations additionally incurs their representation, reading, and covariance-formation cost, including at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) record operations. The statistical theorem remains exact-real at the sampling layer. Its encoder guarantee is distance to a unit-row parent-supported range class, not invertibility, a unique repeated-eigenspace representative, or latent-coordinate error independent of the mixing map. The positive guarantee is specific to Gaussian variance resets and does not transfer to the full published soft-intervention class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The positive statistical and polynomial-bit post-summary theorems concern the linear Gaussian perfect variance-reset subclass in fixed coordinates on \(\mathcal S\). They target only \(I^{-1}\operatorname{TC}(\mathcal G)I\) and the correspondingly environment-indexed parent-supported encoder range class. The rational algorithm is polynomial after covariance summaries are available; an end-to-end raw-data implementation must also pay at least \(\Omega(B_{\mathrm{tot}})\) to read the sample records, so its runtime is not polynomial only in logarithmic gap parameters. The separation family is legal in Acartürk et al.'s broader smooth soft-intervention class and proves that equation (22)'s all-subset margin is not necessary for recovery there, but it does not promote the Gaussian certificate to that broader class. Actual projector geometry and \(\rho_i(G)\) replace the source's false printed norm-product identity. Neither an invertible encoder nor a canonical representative inside a repeated positive eigenspace is claimed.
